subject.title: [Feature]: Multi-role support in Chat UI for multi-agent workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable per-message sender identity contract for multi-agent conversations, and what canonical fields and trust semantics should flow through protocol, transcripts, live/history events, and Control UI rendering?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow UI bug: it affects public Gateway APIs, session-state persistence, model-facing provenance, trust boundaries, and renderer behavior across existing partial attribution mechanisms.

options.title: Design Additive Sender Identity Contract
options.body: Introduce one canonical per-message identity shape and migrate the existing senderLabel/provenance/UI paths to consume it while preserving compatibility.

options.title: Continue Narrow Attribution Fixes
options.body: Keep fixing specific gaps such as sessions_send requester names or WebChat senderLabel fallbacks without committing to a broad identity contract yet.

options.title: Defer To Broader Multi-Agent Model
options.body: Keep this open until a larger multi-agent conversation and permission model is ready to own sender identity end to end.

recommendation.title: Design Additive Sender Identity Contract
recommendation.body: Introduce one canonical per-message identity shape and migrate the existing senderLabel/provenance/UI paths to consume it while preserving compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans provenance/session contracts and multi-agent UX direction, and steipete is already the strongest routing candidate in the issue discussion and adjacent history.
